stages.name: Instant Activation Eligibility & Serial Verification (INS)
stages.goals: Not found in source — no customer-frame goal statement is present for this stage.
stages.actions: System detects a reusable pre-installed device from the ready-for-service response (FAR_002_INS_01, BR-130); the agent, on a tablet only (FAR_002_INS_07, BR-136), verifies the detected device serial number against the physical device (FAR_002_INS_02, BR-131), then explicitly selects instant or normal activation, defaulting to normal where instant is not selected (FAR_002_INS_03, BR-132).
stages.touchpoints: Retail Store / Field - Retail Agent - Tablet only, physical device serial check (INS)
stages.systems: Ready for Service Portal, Siebel CRM

painPoints.text: Instant activation is available only to field agents on a tablet device; physical device verification is not supported on a desktop-only agent, and a detected device serial mismatch is recorded and may lead to failure of the instant path (BR-136, BR-131, FAR_002_INS_07)

currentResponses.text: No current mitigation documented beyond the channel constraint check itself (BR-136) — a desktop agent simply cannot offer instant activation; no fallback path for a serial mismatch is stated beyond defaulting to normal activation (BR-132)

painPoints.text: Immediate activation targets completion within 30 minutes (P-21, BR-134); where the service is not working after instant activation, the only stated handling is to raise a support request and arrange a technician visit (BR-135, FAR_002_INS_06), meaning the promised speed advantage can revert to a full field visit with no stated interim compensation or communication to the customer

currentResponses.text: System raises a support request and arranges a technician visit on a non-working instant-activated service as the only stated handling; no retry, credit, or proactive customer notification process is documented beyond this (BR-135)

stages.name: Migration Cutover, Failure Recovery & Notification (MIG)
stages.goals: Not found in source — no customer-frame goal statement is present for this stage.
stages.actions: On successful Fibre activation the system deactivates the FWA SIM (FIB_MIG_RTL_003_11, BR-145), terminates the old connection and services, releases FWA resources (FIB_MIG_RTL_003_12, BR-145C), cuts billing over to Fibre from the migration completion date with FWA billing ceasing the same date (FIB_MIG_RTL_003_13, BR-145D), and notifies the customer at request creation, appointment confirmation, migration completion and migration failure (FIB_MIG_RTL_003_14, BR-145E); a failed Fibre migration does not automatically terminate the existing FWA service (FIB_MIG_RTL_003_15, BR-145F).

painPoints.text: Where a request is routed through Retention, a retention outcome is mandatory before the customer can proceed to terminate, and any early-termination or lock-in penalty (plan lock-in is 3 months per the CAF) is calculated and shown at this stage, both of which can add friction or cost the customer had not anticipated when requesting termination
